reasons: The candidate multiplies the result by a constant 100 that does not appear in the Datadog source, which changes the values and violates the no-invented-constants rule.

The Datadog query filters by the host template variable ($host with tag prefix host, default *), but the candidate PromQL has no host matcher, so the series set is not filtered the same way. The dataset observes no host label for redis.db.keys, so the correct label name cannot be confirmed from the given data.

The base metric redis.db.keys (gauge, unit {key}, summed over db) does measure the same quantity as redis.keys, and the sum aggregation matches, so a translated outcome is correct once the constant is removed and the host matcher is added.
